items.text: This wine bar concept requires a Conditional Use Authorization for bar use and a Place of Entertainment permit, both discretionary hearings whose outcomes the records do not settle, and sits in a high-density alcohol corridor where ABC will likely require a Public Convenience or Necessity finding f…
Planning Code §762 classifies Bar as a conditional use (C) on the first story in NCT-VALENCIA zoning district, requiring a Conditional Use Authorization from the Planning Commission.

The Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District (§249.60) permits a new or relocated Bar only as a conditional use and only if the operator uses a liquor license transferred from another Bar within the SUD.
An active ABC Type 41 (on-sale beer and wine, eating place) license is on file at 995 Valencia St, issued November 3, 2023 to Sarita's Grill & Beer.

In 2011 Planning approved CUA 2011.0255C to change an existing full-service restaurant at 991-999 Valencia St from a Type 41 to a Type 47 license, demonstrating that this address has been approved for alcohol service but as a restaurant use.

Only 3 dated use decisions for bar-type businesses were found within 1,000 ft in the last 10 years (N=3): 1 approved, 0 approved with conditions, 0 denied, 2 withdrawn, which is too few to establish an approval rate.

A CUA application for a bar within a full-service restaurant at 970-974 Valencia St (66 m away, NCT-VALENCIA) was withdrawn in January 2011, and a CUA for a restaurant with Type 41 and live entertainment at 2519 Mission St (210 m, NCT-MISSION) was withdrawn in October 2019.

ABC Type 42 (on-sale beer and wine, public premises) is a non-quota license that ABC issues directly, but nearly every city treats Type 42 as a bar use requiring conditional use or police/planning review before ABC will issue.

The census tract shows 51 active on-sale ABC licenses within 1,000 ft of 995 Valencia St, flagged for undue concentration; at this density ABC will require a Public Convenience or Necessity (PCN) finding from the City.

Nine active on-sale licenses exist within 500 ft of this address, including one Type 41 at 995 Valencia (the current tenant), two Type 47 licenses, one Type 21 off-sale, and five additional Type 41 licenses at nearby restaurants.
ABC's timeline for a Type 42 is typically 60-120 days if unprotested, but local protests or undue-concentration findings add 1-3 months for the PCN process.

A Place of Entertainment permit is required when entertainment is a primary use or when live music or amplified sound runs until 2 am; this concept's live music and amplified sound operating until 1 am falls within that requirement.
Amados at 998 Valencia St (31 m away) holds an active Place of Entertainment permit and operates with a Type 47 license in NCT-VALENCIA within the Mission Alcohol SUD.
Planning recommended approval of a POE permit accessory to retail use at 998 Valencia in May 2014, limited to 1/3 of the floor area and conforming to Police Code §1060(r).
Arcana SF at 2512 Mission St (150 m away, NCT-MISSION) holds an active POE permit for restaurant and nighttime entertainment use, approved by Planning referral in November 2020.
POE applications require a $2,708 fee (2026-27), Police and Planning review, a 30-day posted notice at the site, and a public hearing before the Entertainment Commission; timelines run 45-120 days.

Nearby POE permits have been approved when entertainment is framed as accessory or secondary to a primary food-service or retail use, with conditions on hours, sound levels, and good-neighbor policies.

Any food facility with a kitchen needs a DPH Health Permit to Operate, which requires plan check approval, a certified food safety manager on staff, and a final inspection confirming the facility matches approved plans before the permit is issued.

DPH plan check for a new or remodeled kitchen costs $828-$2,207 (2026-27) depending on scope, with review times of 21-60 days; the Permit to Operate application fee is $470 and the annual license fee for restaurants is $0 for 2026-28.
A DPH referral at 995 Valencia St in January 2021 recommended approval of continuation of restaurant use per §102 and §762, citing Conditional Use authorization Motion No. 18363.
Planning referrals for limited-restaurant health permits have been approved at 3285 21st St (32 m away) in 2018, at 956 Valencia St (72 m) in 2017, and at 1014 Valencia St (79 m) in 2017.

Kitchen build-outs, hoods, restrooms, and ADA upgrades need a DBI building permit with plans stamped by an architect; full plan review with Planning, Fire, Public Health, and PUC routing takes 2-4 months, and fees are a percentage of construction valuation.
A DPH referral at 995 Valencia St in January 2021 confirmed continuation of restaurant use per §102 and §762, referencing prior Conditional Use authorization Motion No. 18363.

Agency referrals at this address dating to 1999 approved large full-service restaurant use and Type 41 licenses accessory to restaurant use; the most recent ABC license (Type 41, issued November 2023) is for Sarita's Grill & Beer.

Any new food facility or kitchen remodel affecting layout, equipment, or finishes needs DPH plan check approval; the plan must be routed to DPH as part of the building permit application and approved before construction begins.

Expected condition: Hours of operation limited to 6 am to 1 am (or earlier closing hour such as midnight on weeknights) with no extended-hours service. Basis: Planning Code §762 table allows hours 6 am-2 am as principally permitted and 2 am-6 am as conditional in NCT-VALENCIA. Nearby approved POE permits and restaurant CUAs in the Mission and Valencia corridors typically condition closing hours to 1 am or midnight to mitigate noise and late-night impacts, though specific conditions for this address are not extracted.

Expected condition: Sound-level limits and soundproofing requirements to prevent noise transmission to neighboring residential units, with periodic sound monitoring and a complaint-response protocol. Basis: POE permits routinely include conditions on amplified sound, bass frequencies, and sound insulation when residential units are upstairs or adjacent. The catalog notes that sound complaints from upstairs residents are the main reason POE permits are conditioned or denied, and recommends commissioning an acoustic report before the hearing.

Expected condition: Compliance with the Entertainment Commission's Good Neighbor Policy, including a written plan addressing noise, queuing, sidewalk management, security, and a designated community liaison. Basis: Recent POE approvals and Planning's Project Profile Lite for a nightclub at 2500 Mission St (2026) cite the Entertainment Commission's Good Neighbor Policy as a standard condition for entertainment uses.

Expected condition: ABC license restricted to beer and wine service only (Type 42), with no spirits or full-bar service unless a Type 47 or Type 48 license is obtained and approved by Planning. Basis: The concept profile specifies beer and wine only, and the catalog confirms that Type 42 covers on-sale beer and wine at public premises. Any upgrade to full liquor would require a quota license (Type 47 or 48) and a new or amended CUA.

Expected condition: Security plan detailing staffing, ID checks, queue management, and procedures to prevent over-service and manage patron behavior, particularly after 10 pm. Basis: Entertainment Commission POE permits and Planning CUAs for bar and late-night uses commonly require security plans. The high density of bars and the undue-concentration flag suggest both agencies will scrutinize public-safety measures.

Expected condition: No dancing allowed unless the POE permit explicitly authorizes it; if dancing is proposed later, an amended POE application and potentially an amended CUA will be required. Basis: The concept profile states no dancing, and the catalog distinguishes POE permits (which cover live entertainment and amplified sound) from nightclub uses that include dancing. Any material change adding dancing would trigger new discretionary review.

You will receive a Business Account Number (BAN) that every other city department requires. File the FBN statement in person or by mail with the County Clerk (with photo ID), then publish it once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper and file proof of publication within 45 days. Banks and ABC want the filed DBA statement.
